page: Amazon Web Services c4.large is a compute-optimized instance belonging to the fourth-generation c4 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor operating at 2.9 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 4.0 GB of system memory. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and relies on a Xen hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but limited multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance registers at 1478.68, and single-threaded gzip compression achieves 24.27 GB/sec, both falling into average tiers. However, multi-core metrics are constrained, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1945.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1368.0, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth is also low, measuring 13.03 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 11.47 GB/sec for write operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.large offers dedicated CPU allocation for compute-focused workloads without the overhead of larger instances, though its older hardware generation limits overall resource density. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled local storage and weak multi-threaded scaling. It is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, single-threaded batch processing, basic web serving, and small-scale utility workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but do not demand high memory capacity or rapid multi-core execution.
